window: Covering reporting published since the Sept 19 edition, roughly Sept 18-20, with the Catonsville, Maryland indictment and the Paraná, Brazil highway seizures running back to incident dates of Sept 17 where reporting lagged. A new SOUTHCOM/JTF-WHEM lethal strike on Sept 19 killed four people; same-day wire tallies (USNews, local10, The Hindu via AP) put the campaign's running total at 69 strikes and at least 231 deaths, which is the figure used below rather than arithmetically adding to the prior edition's carried 69/230 count, since independent trackers' cumulative strike counts have varied by a few in past editions and today's post-strike figures are the freshest available. Several candidate stories were dropped as stale on verification: a Buncombe County, NC 'largest fentanyl seizure in BCSO history' story recirculating this week was actually an April 16 incident; an Upshur County, TX meth/fentanyl ring dismantling was from a January case; a Garfield Heights, OH gun-and-drug stop and an Oregon 110,000-plant marijuana raid were both over a week outside the window; a Paranaguá, Brazil 226-kg cocaine seizure was from March; a Santa Catarina/São Paulo 521-kg Brazilian cocaine case was from Sept 5-6; and a Bolivian FELCN Uyuni marijuana find and a Chilean La Serena 10-kg marijuana interception were both too thin (no confirmed weight or below the size bar) to carry. Colombia's own same-day figures were internally inconsistent — a single Guaviare naval operation reported 975 kg of cocaine, more than the government's separate nationwide 24-hour tally of 900 kg of cocaine — so only the specific, sourced Guaviare figure is counted in today's tally rather than the vaguer aggregate. A Panama Chiriquí seizure of 5,529 packages is included without a seizures entry because Panamanian authorities did not confirm the drug type or weight, despite outlets estimating roughly 5.5 tonnes of cocaine from typical package sizes.
